# frontend/admin

The management backend uses pnpm workspace, organized by "thin host + core base + optional business modules + engineering tools". The host is only responsible for combination and startup; pages, requests, RPC types and business dependencies belong to the corresponding module package.
The System module contains message management, message classification and personal inbox, and displays unread messages through the top tool.
Core layout provides lock screen capabilities in the avatar menu, and the lock screen password digest is only persisted during the current lock screen session.

The dependency direction is fixed to `app -> business module -> core`. The core does not depend on any business modules, and business modules do not reference each other by default; when reuse is really needed, they can only use the Interface exposed by the other party `package.json#exports`.

## Directory Responsibilities

```text
frontend/admin
├── apps/admin                        # 装配当前全部 module 的默认宿主
├── packages/core                     # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-core 底座
│   ├── src/api/{base/v1,system/admin/v1} # 按 Proto 完整路径组织的底座请求
│   ├── src/components                # 公共组件
│   ├── src/layouts                   # 布局
│   ├── src/modules                   # 模块注册 interface
│   ├── src/rpc                       # 登录、菜单和底座能力 Proto 类型
│   └── src/views                     # 登录与静态错误页面
├── packages/modules/system           # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-system
│   └── src/{api,config,rpc,utils,views} # API 与 RPC 按 Proto 层级维护
├── packages/cli                      # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli
│   └── templates/business-workspace  # 完整 pnpm workspace 模板
├── internal/vite-config              # 当前仓库宿主构建配置
├── internal/tsconfig                 # 共享 TypeScript 配置
├── internal/lint-config              # 共享 Oxlint 配置
├── scripts/build-package.mjs          # core 与业务模块的 npm 发布构建器
├── package.json                       # workspace 命令与公共开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── tsconfig.json                      # workspace TypeScript 路径映射
└── turbo.json
```

`apps/admin/src/module-manifest.ts` is the only source of default host module configuration, and declares the runtime loader, Vite scanning package and pre-built dependencies; `apps/admin/src/modules.ts` loads and exports all modules of the current host by default. Core's business view directory only retains the login page. 403, 404, 500, and Pending are provided by core with default static implementations; the personal center, AI assistant, and system management pages are all provided by `systemAdminModule`. The personal center and AI assistant dynamically register routes through the backend menu and do not declare static business routes in the host.

## Root directory file

| path | function |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/` | A collection of runnable management hosts; the current default host is `admin`.                  |
| `packages/core/` | Publishable admin runtime, layouts, components and base pages.                      |
| `packages/modules/` | A collection of optional business modules. APIs and pages are maintained together within the module.                    |
| `packages/cli/` | Publishable standalone business workspace command line tools and templates.                     |
| `internal/` | Vite, TypeScript and lint configuration packages for the current source code repository only.          |
| `scripts/build-package.mjs` | Generate a copy of the npm package source code and TypeScript declaration, and convert core internal source code aliases. |
| `package.json` | Declare workspace-level commands, tool dependencies, Node and pnpm versions.              |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Fixed dependency resolution results for the entire workspace.                               |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | Declares the workspace package under `apps`, `packages`, and `internal`.         |
| `tsconfig.json` | Inherit the shared configuration and declare the source code path mapping of this warehouse.                            |
| `turbo.json` | Defines development, build, release build, and type checking task relationships.                      |
| `AGENTS.md` | Collaboration and code constraints of the management directory.                                      |
| `.editorconfig` | General editor indentation, line wrapping, and character set rules.                                |
| `.gitignore` | Management-side local product ignores rules.                                          |
| `.oxlintignore` | Oxlint scan exclusion rules.                                             |
| `.prettierignore`, `.prettierrc.cjs` | Prettier exclusion range and format configuration.                                     |
| `.stylelintignore`, `.stylelintrc.cjs` | Stylelint exclude scope and style rules.                                    |
| `lint-staged.config.cjs` | Management-side temporary file check configuration used by warehouse-level Git hook.                    |
| `commitlint.config.cjs` | Git submission information verification rules.                                            |
| `postcss.config.cjs` | PostCSS and browser prefix handling configuration.                                    |
| `README.md` | workspace architecture, public commands and module access instructions.                          |

Each subdirectory containing `package.json` has a sibling `README.md`, which describes the package's internal file and directory responsibilities.

The management side publishes `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core`, `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system` and
`@liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli`. The default host `@liujitcn/kratos-admin` is a private package and cannot be entered.
npm packaging and distribution manifest.

## Development and Construction

```bash
cd frontend/admin
pnpm install
pnpm dev
pnpm test
pnpm type:check
pnpm lint:oxlint
pnpm build
pnpm build:package
```

In the `frontend/admin` directory, you can also execute common processes through the upper-level Makefile:

```bash
make -C .. run-admin
make -C .. check-admin
make -C .. build-admin
make -C .. package-admin
```

The default host address is `http://localhost:8848`. The environment variable is located at `apps/admin/.env*`. The development mode API agent and production build output directory are managed uniformly by the host Vite configuration; the current production build is written to `backend/data/admin`.

The management-side login password is encrypted by Web Crypto in the security context; when accessed through the LAN HTTP address and the browser does not have Web Crypto, it will fall back to the pure JavaScript implementation and keep the back-end password ciphertext protocol unchanged. This rollback only addresses operational compatibility. HTTP may still expose tokens or be subject to active tampering. Please use HTTPS in production environments.

This machine enables HTTPS development services through LAN IP:

```bash
cd ../..
bash scripts/generate-dev-cert.sh 192.168.1.100
```

Replace the above IP with the actual LAN IP of the machine. The script will generate a shared certificate in the repository root `certs`; then add `VITE_HTTPS=true` to `apps/admin/.env.development.local`. After restarting `pnpm dev` and accessing `https://192.168.1.100:8848`, you need to accept the local self-signed certificate in the browser for the first time; other devices also need to trust the certificate when accessing. Backend, Taro and uni-app can reuse certificates in the same directory.

The management-side authentication status adopts the browser Cookie-only mode: the refresh token is written by the backend to the HttpOnly Cookie with the narrowed Path. The access token is only saved in the page memory and is not written to `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`. When the application starts, it will proactively clean up the persistent access tokens left behind by the old version, and use non-sensitive expiration time cookies to determine whether the session needs to be restored silently.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by the management end are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The language key and placeholder set are verified when registering the module. The login page and the top toolbar share the locale store. Switching languages ​​does not refresh the page, and retains the current routing, query parameters, and unsubmitted forms.

语言偏好保存为 `kratos-admin:locale`。 Axios, refresh token, native fetch, SSE and Swagger requests uniformly send `Accept-Language`; dynamic menus and dictionaries are returned by the backend by locale, and fall back to the main language when the current language translation is missing. To add a new language, you need to synchronize the back-end internationalization directory and the six front-end language package directories of the three workspaces, and then execute `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory; the registration file and Day.js mapping are generated by the script.具体流程见 [国际化语言扩展指南](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md)。

The API is organized into directories such as `api/base/v1` and `api/system/admin/v1` according to the full path of Proto. `src/api` only retains the request package with the same name as the service file; the running configuration and internal auxiliary implementation are placed in `src/config` and `src/utils` respectively. RPC retains the complete Proto hierarchy of `rpc/base/v1`, `rpc/system/admin/v1`, etc. RPC types are placed according to real consumer ownership: core retains login, menu, user information and service types required during startup capabilities; System self-contained system management, personal center, AI and its dependency types. After modifying Proto, execute `make -C frontend ts-admin` in the root directory of the warehouse. The command will clean and generate RPCs for core and system according to the two Buf configurations; execute it when you need to generate RPCs for three front-ends at once.`make -C frontend ts`. When the server-side contract has not completed fine-grained splitting, the same generated file may temporarily contain methods that are not called by the current package, and the generated file is not manually written.

The core internal source code uses `@/*`; the business module uses `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/*` and its own package name. Vue Router is used for page jumps between modules, and cross-directory relative references are prohibited for code reuse.

The root TypeScript path and host Vite source code alias only map the entrance declared by `package.json#exports` for each npm package; the core implementation uses `@/*` internally, and the business module uses the package name to reference the public entrance.

## module interface

core exports `bootstrapAdminApp`, `defineAdminModule`, `setAdminDocumentTitle`, view registry, and top tool, user menu, and routing behavior extensions. The browser title preferentially uses `sysName` returned by the public configuration interface, and the host environment variable is used as a fallback when loading fails. The business module entrance declares the name and page loader to access the dynamic page:

```ts
import type { Component } from "vue";
import { defineAdminModule } from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core";

const views = import.meta.glob<{ default: Component }>("./views/**/*.vue");

export const orderAdminModule = defineAdminModule({
  name: "order",
  views
});
```

The business page only registers the module prefix path, so `views/list/index.vue` is uniformly parsed by `order/list/index`, and the `list/index` unprefixed alias is not provided. The complete module path must be written in `component` of the backend menu; different modules will not overwrite each other even if they contain `views` pages with the same name. The host declares the module in `src/module-manifest.ts`, `src/modules.ts` loads and exports all modules by default, and the Vite build configuration is derived from the manifest:

```ts
export const adminModuleManifest = [
  {
    packageName: "@order/admin-module",
    load: async () => (await import("@order/admin-module")).orderAdminModule
  }
];
```

### Replace static page

core exposes the fixed view keys of all static pages through `ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS`:

| Properties | View Keys |
| -------------- | --------------- |
| `LOGIN` | `login/index` |
| `FORBIDDEN` | `error/403` |
| `NOT_FOUND` | `error/404` |
| `SERVER_ERROR` | `error/500` |
| `PENDING` | `error/pending` |

The business module explicitly maps any of its pages to fixed view keys through `staticViews`, and the later registration module replaces the first registration implementation:

```ts
import { ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS, defineAdminModule } from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core";

export const orderAdminModule = defineAdminModule({
  name: "order",
  staticViews: {
    [ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS.NOT_FOUND]: () => import("./components/NotFound.vue"),
    [ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS.PENDING]: () => import("./components/Pending.vue")
  }
});
```

Ordinary `views` is always isolated by module name, only `staticViews` is replaceable Seam. The npm Interface of core only exposes module access, component whitelist, and stable entrances such as `request`, `navigation`, `table`, `security`, `stores/runtime`; business modules must not rely on the internal source code path of core.

## Create business project

The business project generated by the CLI itself is also a pnpm workspace, including an independent host and a publishable business module package:

```bash
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli create shop-admin --module shop
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli create shop-admin --module shop,order

# 当前仓库开发
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop,order
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop --module order
```

Generates results:

```text
shop-admin
├── apps/admin
│   └── README.md
├── packages/modules/shop
│   └── README.md
├── packages/modules/order
│   └── README.md
├── scripts/build-package.mjs
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── README.md
├── tsconfig.json
└── turbo.json
```

By default, CLI imports `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system` first, and then imports and creates its own module according to the `--module` parameter sequence. `--module` is reusable and also accepts comma-separated names; `--with` only adds additional published modules to the host portfolio, without creating their source code or creating implicit dependencies between business modules. The CLI refuses to overwrite an existing directory.

# frontend/taro-app

`frontend/taro-app` is an independent pnpm workspace, using React 18 and Taro 4 to implement the same application functionality and vision as `frontend/uni-app`. Currently supports H5 and WeChat mini programs, including home page, login (including TOTP/WebAuthn MFA), protocol, WebView, personal center, settings, personal information, AI assistant and on-site email inbox, but does not include mall, order, payment or recommendation services.

## Workspace

```text
frontend/taro-app
├── apps/taro-app                 # 私有 Taro 宿主，不发布
├── packages/core                 # 运行时、基础页面和构建 runner
├── packages/ui                   # NutUI 主题与按需图标适配
├── packages/modules/system       # 个人中心、设置、资料和 AI
├── packages/cli                  # 独立 workspace 脚手架
├── scripts                       # package exports 边界检查
├── package.json                  # 公共命令和开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml           # workspace 包范围
└── turbo.json                    # 跨包任务依赖
```

The dependency direction is fixed to:

```text
apps/taro-app -> packages/modules/* -> packages/ui -> packages/core
```

core does not depend on UI or business modules; system only has reusability through the core and UI's public exports; the host is only responsible for combining modules and platform configuration.

Detailed description:

- [Private host ](apps/taro-app/README.md)
- [Application base ](packages/core/README.md)
- [UI Basic Package ](packages/ui/README.md)
- [system module ](packages/modules/system/README.md)
- [Project Scaffolding ](packages/cli/README.md)

## Page assembly

`apps/taro-app/src/module-manifest.ts` is the only module manifest, the declaration order determines the override priority for pages, stable `viewKey` and icons. The module declares runtime capabilities through `defineKratosTaroModule()` and exposes build-time page descriptions through `defineKratosTaroBuildModule()`.

The host only submits the fixed `pages/bootstrap` page. The core runner completes the following operations before development or build begins:

- Scan each module for `src/views/**/*.tsx`, ignoring `components` at any level.
- Generate page wrapper and page config, mount the self-drawn `KratosTabBar` uniformly, and complete the top bar consistent with uni-app for the H5 default navigation page.
- Split main package and sub-package by `pages*` root directory.
- Merge each module `src/static` to the host. Files already in the host will be given priority, and files with the same name as modules will be registered first.
- Restore original `app.config.ts` and delete temporary files after build exit.

The page wrapper uniformly mounts the self-drawn `KratosTabBar`; the fixed homepage and my page are registered as hidden native tab routes at the same time. `switchTab` is used when switching to maintain the WeChat native effect, dynamically expand the tab and then reuse the page stack. Ordinary pages use `navigateTo` first, and subordinate pages will belong along the parent relationship and highlight the corresponding tab.

After exiting abnormally, the next command will be automatically restored based on `.kratos-taro-app-pages-state.json`. H5 and WeChat applet development processes can hold the same page assembly transaction at the same time; the runner will only restore the host file after all processes exit. The default product directories for the two targets are `dist/h5` and `dist/mp-weixin`.

## Development and Construction

```bash
cd frontend/taro-app
pnpm install
pnpm dev:h5
pnpm dev:mp-weixin
pnpm build:h5
pnpm build:mp-weixin
```

The upper-level Frontend Makefile provides the corresponding aggregation entry:

```bash
make -C .. run-taro-app      # 微信小程序开发
make -C .. check-taro-app
make -C .. build-taro-app    # H5 构建
make -C .. package-taro-app
```

- The default H5 development address is `http://localhost:5002`, `/api` and `/events` proxy to `http://localhost:7001`.
- When H5 is accessed through LAN IP, first run `bash scripts/generate-dev-cert.sh 192.168.1.100` in the warehouse root directory to generate a shared certificate, and then set `VITE_APP_HTTPS=true` in `.env.development-h5.local`; if the backend uses `APP_ENV=https`, change `VITE_APP_API_URL` to `https://localhost:7001` at the same time. The certificate reads the repository roots `certs/dev-key.pem` and `certs/dev-cert.pem` by default.
- H5 production product is written to `backend/data/taro-app`, and the access address is `/taro-app/`.
- WeChat applet development and production products are uniformly written into `apps/taro-app/dist/mp-weixin`, and WeChat developer tools can be directly imported into this directory.
- The environment file is located in the workspace root directory, and the variable names are consistent with uni-app: `VITE_APP_PORT`, `VITE_APP_BASE_PATH`, `VITE_APP_BASE_API`, `VITE_APP_API_URL`, `VITE_APP_STATIC_API`, `VITE_APP_STATIC_URL`. H5 will overlay `.env.development-h5` or `.env.production-h5` on the base mode file.
- `KRATOS_TARO_OUTPUT_ROOT` is only used to override the build output directory and is not an API environment variable.

The design width is 750. `rpx` migrated from uni-app is directly written as Taro design draft `px`; the original `px` of physical pixels must be maintained and written using Taro without conversion.

Packaged resources that require fixed paths within the module are placed in `src/static`. Images directly displayed on the page are statically imported through the `static/*` export of the corresponding package, such as `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-core/static/images/avatar.png`, to ensure that Webpack generates correct references in H5 and WeChat page chunks; `resolveBundledAsset('static/...')` is only used for runtime paths such as dynamic menu icons that cannot be statically imported.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by Taro are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The key and placeholder set are verified when registering the module; the login, homepage, status page, WebView, personal center, settings, information and AI pages all use fixed copywriting through `t(key)`. The language preference is saved as `kratos-app:locale`, and the stable routing and business fields will not change after switching.

All `Taro.request`, file upload, and SSE requests are sent to `Accept-Language`. The dynamic menu follows the title parsed by the backend and falls back to the main language when the current language translation is missing; to add a new language, you need to synchronize the backend internationalization directory and the six front-end language pack directories of the three workspaces, and then execute `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory. For the specific process, see [International Language Expansion Guide ](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md).

## RPC generation

Taro RPC templates are unified at `backend/api`:

- `buf.taro-app.typescript.gen.yaml` generates core RPC.
- `buf.taro-app.core.typescript.gen.yaml` generates system RPC.

```bash
pnpm generate:rpc
# 等价于
make -C .. ts-taro-app
```

RPC is a generated product and cannot be modified manually.

## CLI

```bash
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create my-app
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create shop-app --module shop,order
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create my-app --with @acme/customer-module
```

The generated project follows the same React/Taro technology stack, module list, runner transaction protocol and H5/WeChat construction method. The local module independently maintains `pages`, runtime entrance and construction period entrance, which is suitable for subsequent adding capabilities to the mall by business domain.

## Package and Verification

The 4 public package versions must be consistent:

- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-core`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-ui`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-system`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli`

```bash
pnpm lint
pnpm tsc
pnpm test
pnpm check:exports
pnpm build:packages
pnpm build:h5
pnpm build:mp-weixin
```

`check:exports` validates public targets, version consistency and cross-package import boundaries; `test` overrides modules covering priorities, navigation, runner transactions, CLI scaffolding and AI SSE; `build:packages` generates 4 tarballs at `dist/npm`.

# frontend/uni-app

`frontend/uni-app` is an independent pnpm workspace that provides directly runnable uni-app host, publishable application base, system business module and project scaffolding. The technology stack is `uni-app + Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite + Pinia + Sass` and currently supports H5 and WeChat mini programs.

The application side only reuses the layering idea of ​​the management side and does not rely on the source code or workspace of `frontend/admin`. Currently, the homepage, login (including TOTP/WebAuthn MFA), protocol, WebView, personal center, settings (including MFA binding), personal information, AI assistant, and site mail inbox are retained, and does not include the mall, order, payment, or recommendation services.

## Workspace

```text
frontend/uni-app
├── apps
│   └── uni-app                # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app，默认宿主，不发布
│       ├── src
│       │   ├── pages/bootstrap
│       │   ├── module-manifest.ts
│       │   ├── manifest.json
│       │   └── pages.json
│       ├── README.md
│       └── package.json
├── packages
│   ├── core                   # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core v0.0.29
│   │   ├── src                # 底座运行时、页面、状态和构建插件
│   │   ├── test
│   │   ├── README.md
│   │   └── package.json
│   ├── modules
│   │   └── system             # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-system v0.0.29
│   │       ├── src            # 个人中心、默认设置包装和 AI
│   │       ├── README.md
│   │       └── package.json
│   └── cli                    # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-cli v0.0.29
│       ├── bin
│       ├── src
│       ├── test
│       ├── README.md
│       └── package.json
├── scripts                    # 包导出边界检查
├── README.md                  # workspace 总览和公共命令
├── package.json               # workspace 脚本与公共开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml        # workspace 包范围
└── turbo.json                 # 跨包任务依赖与缓存配置
```

The dependency direction is fixed to:

```text
@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app
  -> @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-system
  -> @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core
```

- `core` is responsible for authentication, requests, configuration, Pinia, public settings page, base page, status page, dynamic navigation and building plugins.
- `system` is responsible for the personal center, profile, default settings packaging and AI page, and only reuses base capabilities through `core`'s public exports.
- `apps/uni-app` only maintains the host entry, manifest, module list, bootstrap page and Vite configuration.
- `cli` Create a separate pnpm workspace with the same structure.

For the directory boundaries, functions and public entries of each package, see:

- [Host application ](apps/uni-app/README.md)
- [Application base ](packages/core/README.md)
- [system module ](packages/modules/system/README.md)
- [Project Scaffolding ](packages/cli/README.md)

The workspace root directory no longer retains the `src`, `bin` or empty template directories of the old single application. The business source code can only be located in the corresponding host or package.

## Page assembly

The host maintains a unique module list at `apps/uni-app/src/module-manifest.ts`, and the order determines the static view override priority:

```ts
export const moduleManifest = [coreModule, systemModule]
```

Each module uses the `defineKratosAppModule()` declaration:

- `pages`: Page styling and optional physical routing overrides.
- `views`: Stable mapping of `viewKey` to physical pages.
- `icons`: In-module icons that can be referenced by dynamic navigation.

The build plug-in automatically scans the `src/views/**/*.vue` of each module and ignores the `components` directory at any level. A post-registration module can replace the previous module's static page with the same physical route or `viewKey`.

Host `pages.json` only submits fixed bootstrap pages. During development or construction, the plug-in will temporarily generate page wrappers, merge page configurations, and merge module static files into the host file by file; host files with the same name are given priority, and transactions only record and clean files actually written by the plug-in. Automatically resumes after exiting normally. If the process is forcibly terminated, the previous transaction will be restored based on `.kratos-uni-app-pages-state.json` at the next startup. The same host allows only one H5 or applet development/building process to hold page transactions at the same time. The current process needs to be stopped before switching platforms.

## Dynamic Navigation

The default menu interface is consistent with the management side `base-menu` service:

```text
GET /api/v1/app/base/menu
```

The requested service path is `/v1/app/base/menu`, which is spliced ​​from the unified `/api` base. `base_menu.id = 99000000` is a hidden fixed root directory on the mobile terminal. The backend queries the activation page below it layer by layer and maintains a flat response. Core then presses `parent_id` to build a menu tree; you can also access a custom menu data source through `setAppNavigationAdapter()`. The root directory is only associated with mobile menu queries, and each page menu is associated with the protected API actually called by the page.

Menu configuration constraints:

- `path` uses the `app/` prefix and supports `:参数` and query.
- `name` uses the `App` prefix.
- Title and main icon use `meta.title`, `meta.icon`, icon can use HTTPS address or key registered in module `icons`.
- The mobile configuration is placed in `meta.app` without adding independent table fields.
- `meta.app.view_key` must have been registered by the module, and the interface cannot directly deliver any component path.
- `meta.app.access` supports `PUBLIC`, `GUEST_ONLY`, and `AUTHENTICATED`, which are semantically consistent with the management-side login permissions.
- The secondary pages of the root directory are fixed as tabs. The homepage uses `99010000`, mine uses `99090000`, and `99020000` to `99080000` are reserved for business tabs.
- `meta.app.in_tab_bar` of the second-level tab is fixed to true, and the number can only be 0 or 2–5 items; the selected icon uses `meta.app.selected_icon`, and the lower-level page is fixed to non-tab.

The management menu form recursively identifies the entire mobile terminal tree of `99000000`, displays the logical path, logical name, view key, access mode, mobile terminal icon and API permissions of the page; automatically sets tabs according to the level when submitting, and uniformly packages the mobile terminal configuration into the existing `meta.app`.

Navigation configuration is cached separately in anonymous state and login state. The new configuration will be fully verified and then switched atomically; if the remote end fails, the last successful cache of the current identity will be used; if there is no cache, the local default menu will be used.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by uni-app are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The key and placeholder set are verified when registering the module; the login, homepage, status page, WebView, personal center, settings, information and AI pages all use fixed copywriting through `t(key)`. The language preference is saved as `kratos-app:locale`, and the stable routing and business fields will not change after switching.

All `uni.request`, file upload, and SSE requests are sent to `Accept-Language`. The dynamic menu follows the title parsed by the backend and falls back to the main language when the current language translation is missing; to add a new language, you need to synchronize the backend internationalization directory and the six front-end language pack directories of the three workspaces, and then execute `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory. For the specific process, see [International Language Expansion Guide ](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md).

The page wrapper uniformly mounts the self-drawn `KratosTabBar`; the fixed homepage and my page are registered as hidden native tab routes at the same time. `switchTab` is used when switching to maintain the WeChat native effect, dynamically expand the tab and then reuse the page stack. Ordinary pages use `navigateTo` first, and subordinate pages will belong along the parent relationship and highlight the corresponding tab. Therefore, the menu level, logical path and `viewKey` can be adjusted after the interface content changes, without having to write each service route into the host.
